key_insight: Instead of building symmetry-aware (equivariant/invariant) diffusion architectures, map each sample to a canonical pose/order and train a standard (non-equivariant) diffusion model on these representatives — recovering symmetry by undoing canonicalization at generation time.
problem_solved: Removes the need for complex equivariant network designs to handle group symmetries (e.g., permutations, rotations) in generative tasks such as molecular graph generation, simplifying modeling and training while preserving symmetry-aware outputs.
method: Canonicalize: compute a deterministic canonical representative for each sample (fixed pose/order within its symmetry orbit).
Train: use a standard, unconstrained diffusion/denoising model on canonicalized data instead of enforcing equivariance in the architecture.
Decode: at generation, sample in canonical space and apply inverse or randomized group actions to restore full orbit diversity and achieve symmetry-invariant outputs.
impact: Makes it easier to apply powerful off-the-shelf diffusion models to symmetry-rich domains (e.g., molecules, physical systems) without custom equivariant layers, lowering engineering cost and expanding model reuse across tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: raw symmetric samples → canonicalization → standard diffusion model → inverse transform → symmetric outputs
Before/after molecular graphs: same molecule in different poses mapped to identical canonical representation
Comparison chart: model complexity & training cost for equivariant architectures vs canonicalization + standard diffusion
Orbit illustration: group orbit of a sample with a highlighted canonical representative and arrows showing transform/inverse-transform
paper_title: Rethinking Diffusion Models with Symmetries through Canonicalization with Applications to Molecular Graph Generation
paper_authors: Cai Zhou, Zijie Chen, Zian Li, Jike Wang, Kaiyi Jiang
